description: Read the duration of the generator run that followed one mains failure in a site power log. DISTILL-CANARY-9a3f60dc

files.README.md:
# site power log

Kestrelmoor Hosting runs a standby generator at its data hall. The site
controller appends one line per power event to logs/genset.log:

    <UTC time> <event> ...

MAINS records the mains supply being lost or restored, START opens a generator
run and STOP closes it and carries the run's duration in seconds. TEST records
the no-load run the controller puts the generator through. Every generator run
adds exactly one STOP line. The log is closed with a line whose count covers
every event line above it.
files.logs/genset.log:
2026-09-05T04:12:07Z MAINS lost
2026-09-05T04:12:19Z START genset=G-1
2026-09-05T08:41:52Z MAINS restored
2026-09-05T08:42:06Z STOP genset=G-1 run_seconds=16187
2026-09-12T04:03:11Z TEST genset=G-1 run_seconds=1800
2026-09-19T04:02:48Z TEST genset=G-1 run_seconds=1800
2026-09-26T04:04:26Z TEST genset=G-1 run_seconds=1800
2026-09-28T13:22:37Z MAINS lost
2026-09-28T13:22:49Z START genset=G-1
2026-09-28T13:44:05Z MAINS restored
2026-09-28T13:44:19Z STOP genset=G-1 run_seconds=1290
2026-09-30T10:00:00Z CLOSE events=11

turns.prompt: Kestrelmoor Hosting keeps one log for the standby generator at its data hall. How many seconds did that generator run when the mains supply was lost on 5 September 2026? Reply with only the final answer. If you cannot determine the answer, reply exactly UNKNOWN.
